title: Worcester Performing Arts Centre
description:
Worcester City Council (the "Authority") is bringing to the market an excellent opportunity for the redevelopment of the site of the former Scala Theatre and Corn Exchange in the heart of Worcester City Centre to form a Performing Arts Centre (the "Project").

The redevelopment of the Scala and Corn Exchange forms the primary aspect of the Worcester Future High Street Fund (FHSF) redevelopment programme being led by the Authority. Worcester's FHSF programme will transform the northern part of the City Centre into a diverse leisure, cultural, entertainment and residential quarter that will attract younger people and families. Since the 19th century, the Northern Gateway of Worcester City Centre has served as a commercial hub within the City. However, the area has recently been in decline as the number of vacant retail units has increased and footfall has decreased.

The objective of the FHSF programme is to create a vibrant leisure and entertainment quarter adjacent to the high-quality primary retail core providing residents and visitors with an additional attraction and extending the City Centre's overall vibrancy.

The Authority is seeking to appoint a contractor via a two stage tender process to work with them to deliver the construction (and part design) of and deliver the architectural vision for the Project which has already been developed to RIBA Stage 3.

The Authority is seeking a contractor who will work them collaboratively in order to manage risk, cost and quality and who is sensitive to the nature of the Project, its location and the community interest in it.

In addition to the main building work for the Project, the Authority intends for the appointed contractor to also undertake any demolition and enabling works that are required as part of the development of the site in preparation for the main building works. Further details of the contract documents that the successful tenderer will be required to enter into (the "Contracts") are set out in the Procurement Documents

The successful provider will deliver a service that supports people to live a richer and more fulfilled life, including but not limited to having the skills and confidence to maintain a tenancy, access to education and training, and improved physical and mental wellbeing.

title: PL0283 - Shrub Hill Property Advisor - AWARD
description:
This scope is to support WCC select a Development partner for Shrub Hill Industrial Estate, Worcester.
      
      Located in the heart of Worcester City Centre and covering an area of c.14 hectares, the Shrub Hill Quarter is a long-undervalued area with significant untapped potential. Due to its size, location, and strategic connectivity; it is a regionally significant regeneration opportunity which has the potential to underpin the long-term vitality, growth, and identity of Worcester as both a place to live and to work.
      
      The proposed regeneration of Shrub Hill Quarter, Worcester, Worcestershire has the potential to be one of the largest regeneration projects in the region and presents a once in a lifetime opportunity to shape a significant new part of Worcester and create an exemplary mixed-use neighborhood. 
      
      WCC have just completed a consultation on a Supplementary Planning Document (SPD) for the future development of Shrub Hill, Worcester. The purpose was to build upon the Spatial Blueprint they prepared in 2022, establish key planning and design principles across the site, whilst allowing flexibility for the site to be consented in full or part by future developers or investors, who could take forward detailed planning applications within these parameters.
      
      The Advisor will be a key appointment and will lead the evaluation criteria, financial model and negotiation process and final evaluation. They will also provide supporting commercial real estate advice throughout the process.

title: PL0247 - SLR4 Monitoring and Evaluation Report - AWARD
description:
Further Competition under Lot 5 Highways, Traffic and Transport of ESPO Framework 664_21.  
      
      The A4440 Southern Link Road was largely a single carriageway route that was subject to significant congestion and unreliable journey times. Long distance trips used the city center infrastructure to cross Worcester. The upgrade of the route from Whittington to Powick to dual-2 carriageway standard, with associated junction improvements, was assumed to significantly increase the attractiveness of the bypass route making it the route of choice for East West movements.
      
      Following the Department for Transport's (DfT) approval of Full Business Case for the £62.5m scheme on 1 March 2019, the works for delivering the scheme commenced on 4 March 2019. The Southern Link Road Improvements - Phase 4 (SLR4) scheme opened for road users in August 2022.
      
      As part of the SLR4 Full Business Case, a Benefits Plan was created to provide a strategy for assessing the scheme against the Objectives identified. The plan sets out the evaluation strategy for the SLR4 scheme, covering the monitoring of impacts and the approach to determining the projected benefits, impacts and objectives.
       
      Using the Department for Transport (DfT) Monitoring & Evaluation 2012 Guidance, it was established that the SLR4 scheme should follow guidance for 'Enhanced Monitoring" as well as some aspects of the "Fuller Monitoring" where appropriate.
      
      This tender requirement is to appoint a consultancy to undertake the Evaluation Report. The Evaluation Report will assess outcomes and impacts in line with the Benefits Realisation Plan, including qualitative measures. The evaluation plan outlined within this document is therefore considered fit for purpose without being financially onerous.  Furthermore, the evaluation strategy will help determine future transport strategies for the city.  This Evaluation report should also include analysis of wider economic impacts such as number of houses and jobs associated with the scheme, which will be monitored through qualitative stakeholder assessment and Development Application information from District Councils.

title: PL0194 Public Rights of Way Materials Delivery and Handling - AWARD
description:
Worcestershire has around 16,000 individual public rights of way covering 4,600km.  This network, made up of footpaths, bridleways and byways, provides the public with a means of access on foot, horseback, cycle and, on a small number of routes, using motorised vehicles.  The network is used mostly for informal recreation but also in some locations, as important means of accessing shops, schools, places of employment and other services.
      
      Worcestershire County Council has the statutory responsibility to ensure that the county's public rights of way network is properly mapped and maintained and the network is unobstructed and available for use by the public.  This responsibility is managed by the Public Rights of Way (PROW) Team, working with landowners and occupiers, volunteers, probation service and appointed Service Providers. As part of this work, we need to deliver relevant Public Rights of Way furniture and materials to landowners, volunteers and between storage areas. 
      
      Worcestershire is therefore looking to procure a supplier who would be required to deliver materials to landowners, and volunteers and occasionally work sites. The vast majority of this will be within the County of Worcestershire. Due to the rural and remote nature of these sites this may involve needing to drive down un-metaled access roads so the vehicle provided needs to be capable of this, such as a 4x4 pickup and twin axle trailer. Currently the main storage compound is located at Worcester Woods Country Park and a secondary compound is at Lydiate Ash Highway Depot. These locations may be subject to change. Operatives will be required to have a H&S induction for the compounds as well as having a Lone Working Policy and appropriate and relevant insurances .
      
      PLEASE NOTE THIS IS A RESTRICTED TENDER TO INVITED BIDDERS ONLY.
      
      Full information on requirements can be located in the Service Specification in the tender pack provided. Please ensure all documentation uploaded is read in full before completion of submission.
